text: DAE initialization, conservation and constraint drift Compare consistent initialization, an index-one conservation DAE, and an underlying ODE for an index-three pendulum. Comparisons with stored official IDA output are distinguished from newly executed independent ODE references. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-dae-controls-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Consistent initialization and discrete residuals for an index-one DAE Separate initialization, backward-Euler error and residuals on a known positive index-one DAE branch. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless positive branch; differential and algebraic row scales are both one, with the maximum norm. Editorial clarification One authored positive branch and fixed BE runs; no IDA execution or general DAE-solver qualification. Axes for trajectories, states, time or iterations do not represent physical spatial dimensions. Adopted numerical method Use coupled Newton with an Armijo search in the same scaled norm, retaining rather than repairing a singular initial guess. Index reduction, constraint drift and explicit stabilization for a pendulum Derive an explicit ODE from an index-three position constraint and compare drift and stabilization for consistent and inconsistent starts. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries m=L=g=1, initial angle 0.7 and zero angular velocity; off-manifold controls explicitly add radial velocity. Editorial clarification No projection, normalization or SHAKE/RATTLE; no general index-three-solver or symplecticity claim. Axes for trajectories, states, time or iterations do not represent physical spatial dimensions. Adopted numerical method Advance the index-reduced ODE and a critical constraint-error extension with fixed RK4, integrating constraint work at the same stages.
